eras: Disciples of the Apostles, and the first writings after the New Testament.
Martyrs and teachers of the second and third centuries.
The great Fathers of the fourth century
The age of the Creed: the Trinity and the Holy Spirit defended, and the desert in bloom.
Christ, true God and true man; the monks; and the Orthodox faith set out.
Witnesses of the faith among the Arabs, the Slavs and the Turks.

about.didache: The Teaching of the Twelve Apostles: the oldest Christian handbook, on the two ways, Baptism and the Eucharist.
about.clement-rome: Bishop of Rome after the Apostles; his letter calls the Corinthians back to peace and order.
about.ignatius: Bishop of Antioch, disciple of St John; wrote seven letters on his way to martyrdom in Rome.
about.polycarp: Bishop of Smyrna, disciple of St John, martyred by fire in old age.
about.diognetus: A beautiful early defence of the Christian life: Christians are in the world as the soul is in the body.
about.barnabas: An early letter reading the Old Testament in the light of Christ.
about.hermas: Visions, commandments and parables on repentance, read in the early Church.
about.justin: Philosopher who found Christ; defended the faith before the emperors and was martyred in Rome.
about.irenaeus: Bishop of Lyons, disciple of St Polycarp; refuted the Gnostics and taught the apostolic faith.
about.athenagoras: Athenian philosopher who defended the Christians and the resurrection of the body.
about.theophilus: Bishop of Antioch; the first to use the word "Trinity".
about.hippolytus: Teacher in Rome; wrote on Christ and the Antichrist and against the heresies.
about.cyprian: Bishop of Carthage and martyr; on the unity of the Church and the Lord’s Prayer.
about.thaumaturgus: Bishop of Neocaesarea, the Wonderworker; his Creed was given to him by the Mother of God and St John.
about.dionysius-alex: Bishop of Alexandria, called "the Great", pastor in times of persecution and plague.
about.methodius: Bishop and martyr; the Banquet of the Ten Virgins, in praise of purity.
about.athanasius: Archbishop of Alexandria, the pillar of Orthodoxy against Arius; On the Incarnation.
about.ephrem: Deacon of Edessa, the harp of the Spirit; hymns and homilies.
about.aphrahat: The Persian Sage, the earliest Syriac Father whose writings we have.
about.basil: Archbishop of Caesarea; On the Holy Spirit, the Six Days of Creation, the monastic Rules.
about.cyril-jer: Archbishop of Jerusalem; his lectures prepared the newly baptised for the Mysteries.
about.nazianzen: Archbishop of Constantinople, the Theologian; the Five Theological Orations.
about.nyssa: Bishop of Nyssa, brother of St Basil; on the soul, the resurrection and the life of virtue.
about.macarius: The Great, of Egypt: the Fifty Spiritual Homilies on prayer and the heart.
about.hilary: Bishop of Poitiers, the Athanasius of the West; On the Trinity.
about.ambrose: Bishop of Milan; on the Mysteries, the Holy Spirit, and the duties of the clergy.
about.chrysostom: Archbishop of Constantinople, the Golden Mouth; homilies on the whole New Testament.
about.augustine: Bishop of Hippo; the Confessions, the City of God and his homilies on the Psalms and St John.
about.cassian: Brought the wisdom of the Egyptian desert to the West; the Conferences and the Institutes.
about.cyril-alex: Archbishop of Alexandria; defended the Mother of God and the one Christ at Ephesus.
about.leo: Pope of Rome; his Tome was received at Chalcedon: "Peter has spoken through Leo".
about.vincent: Monk of Lérins: the faith "believed everywhere, always and by all".
about.gregory-dialogist: Pope of Rome; the Pastoral Rule, the Dialogues and the Morals on Job.
about.isaac: Bishop of Nineveh, the Syrian; on stillness, prayer and the mercy of God.
about.damascene: Monk of Mar Saba; The Fount of Knowledge, with its Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith.
about.cyril-phil: Equal-to-the-Apostles, Enlightener of the Slavs with his brother St Methodius; he defended the Holy Trinity before Muslim scholars at the caliph’s court.
about.abu-qurrah: Bishop of Harran and Arabic-speaking teacher of the Orthodox faith; he answered Muslims in their own language.
about.palamas: Archbishop of Thessalonica, teacher of prayer and of the uncreated light; a captive of the Turks, he spoke with them about Christ.
about.councils: The Creed of Nicaea and Constantinople, and the decrees and canons of the Councils.
about.chesterton: English writer, not an Orthodox Christian (an Anglican, later a Roman Catholic). In Orthodoxy he tells how he came to believe the Creed, the faith of the Church, as the truest answer to the riddles of life.
